steps.title: fight the Warden
steps.expected: Section E.1 per-fight record. Aldis leads FIVE -- Burrowback L16, Brooktail L17, Galecrest L17, Meadowhart L18, Tuskroot L20 -- the only full belt the chapter ever fields against the player. MEASURED ARITHMETIC, GATE-F-LEG-S10AB 2026-08-31. combat_math.gd's damage is `power * scale * attack / (attack + defence)`, a RATIO -- so a quick hit lands for about combat.json's `player_quick.power` (9.0) against a comparable defender however high the levels are, while max HP keeps climbing with level. Logged from the run: a L20 Terrapup hit a L15 Trailpup for 8.9-10.7 a time, and the gauntlet's creatures carry 176-270 HP each. That is 20-28 quick hits PER ENEMY, and the press counts this script shipped with were budgeted well under it. Nothing here inflates the player: the counts below are the shipped numbers' own answer to 'how many hits does this fight take', and they are spread across the belt rather than piled onto one creature.

steps.title: finish the Warden
steps.expected: Section E.1 per-fight record. Tuskroot at L20 is the Warden's ace and the level `tests/test_trainers_data.gd::test_the_critical_path_alone_pays_for_the_warden_ready_level` tunes the whole chapter's XP curve to bring the player LEVEL WITH -- so this is the one fight in the Meadows that is meant to be even. Five of his against five of yours, one pilot each. SWITCHING IS THE FIX, not a bigger number. encounter_director.gd::_on_trainer_round_ended treats the piloted creature fainting as LOSING THE WHOLE BATTLE -- its own comment says so, deliberately -- so a script that pilots one creature through a three-creature team is one faint away from a loss with four healthy creatures still on the belt. That is exactly what happened on the first run of this segment: Ripple fainted to the courtyard's third creature with Gale/Tusk/Dusk untouched at full HP, `defeated_stronghold_courtyard` was never set, and the segment failed on a fight it had nearly won. Cycling the pilot between the trainer's creatures is what a five-creature belt is FOR and what CLAUDE.md's own five-and-only-five rule is built around, so the fights below rotate through it.

steps.observation: T2-GATEF-RUN6 modal-holds-locomotion audit. A walk that begins while a narrative modal still owns input does not fail as 'a modal is open' -- it fails as 'did not reach', many steps and sometimes many minutes later, which is how X04 lost its whole combat block to 3601 held frames. This assert is diagnostic and changes no behaviour: it turns that silent cascade into one named cause at the point of origin. RIG-25's rule, applied to narrative modals rather than to shop panels.

steps.title: let the ceremony open itself
steps.expected: The ceremony is not opened by a press. READ OFF THE SHIPPED UI, GATE-F-LEG-S10AB 2026-08-31, not guessed. `scripts/ui/tab_creatures.gd`: the ceremony opens ITSELF -- `game_state.gd::_watch_pending_catch()` opens the pause shell on the creatures tab the frame `Game.pending_catch` is set, and there is no prompt to press. `_maybe_begin_release()` then focuses the NEWCOMER's row, which `_fence_choose_focus()` fences so left/right point at themselves and down from the newcomer wraps to belt row 0. `_begin_farewell()` focuses "Keep them", and `_fence_farewell_buttons()` wraps Keep and "Let them go" onto each other vertically -- again with left/right pointing at themselves.
steps._comment_replaced: WHAT THIS REPLACES. The shipped sequence was `press interact` (nothing in the ceremony answers interact), `focus_move right` (fenced to a no-op in every stage of the ceremony), `ui_accept` on the still-focused NEWCOMER row -- which asks 'let the legendary go?' rather than choosing any of the five -- and then `menu_confirm` on the focused button, which is "Keep them" and is wired to `_back_to_choosing()`. Driven faithfully it walks in a circle: nothing is ever released, `Game.pending_catch` is never cleared, and `legendary_settled` -- objective 26/27 -- is never set. The steps below make the choice the one section L.4 calls 'real and permanent': a creature off the belt, for the legendary.
